# technitium_zone_permissions (Resource)

Manages who may view, modify and delete one zone, on top of `technitium_permissions_zones`. The lists set here are the zone's full lists: users and groups left out lose their rights to it. The server always keeps `Administrators` and `DNS Administrators` with full rights, whatever is set: leave them out, or list them with full rights. Destroying the resource leaves the permissions as they are.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "technitium_zone_permissions" "home" {
  zone = technitium_zone.home.zone

  user_permissions = [
    { username = technitium_user.alice.username, can_view = true, can_modify = true, can_delete = false },
  ]

  # Administrators and DNS Administrators always keep full rights on a zone,
  # so only other groups are listed.
  group_permissions = []
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `zone` (String) The zone. Changing it moves the resource to another zone.

### Optional

- `group_permissions` (Attributes Set) The rights of groups on the zone. The server always keeps `Administrators` and `DNS Administrators` with full rights, whatever is set: leave them out, or list them with full rights. Leaving it out keeps the server's. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--group_permissions))
- `user_permissions` (Attributes Set) The rights of individual users on the zone. An empty set removes them; leaving it out keeps the server's. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--user_permissions))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier.

- `name` (String) The group name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import technitium_zone_permissions.home home.example.com
```
